title: Analytical Exposition Text
summary: Critical literacy for expository arguments: thesis statement formulation, evidence-based argument staging, connective logic of persuasion, and reiteration of viewpoint.

lessons.title: Argument Structure: Thesis, Multi-Point Arguments, and Reiteration

blocks.html:
The Art of Persuasion: Analytical Exposition Text

An Analytical Exposition Text evaluates an important phenomenon or controversial topic to persuade readers that the author's point of view is valid and logically sound. Rather than commanding readers to act (which is the job of Hortatory Exposition), Analytical Exposition focuses on proving why something is the case.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Opinion Column That Changes Public Minds
blocks.html: When an environmental economist writes a column in the Financial Times arguing that carbon taxes accelerate green technological innovation, they do not merely vent their personal feelings. They construct an Analytical Exposition Text: articulating a clear central thesis, defending it with three robust analytical arguments, and synthesizing the conclusion in a compelling reiteration.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Martin and Rose on Genre and Working with Discourse
blocks.html:
Tokoh: J.R. Martin & David Rose Tahun: 2008 M Krisis: Learners write or analyze persuasive essays without recognizing the structural triad of Thesis, Arguments, and Reiteration.

Systemic functional linguists J.R. Martin and David Rose published Working with Discourse: Meaning Beyond the Clause (2008). They mapped the developmental genre continuum, establishing Analytical Exposition as the foundational genre of academic argumentation and intellectual debate.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Analytical Exposition Triad (Thesis, Arguments, Reiteration)
blocks.html: An Analytical Exposition Text is an argumentative text whose communicative purpose is to persuade the reader that the author's stance on a topic is logically valid and substantiated by evidence. Its macrostructure consists of: Thesis, a series of Arguments (Point + Elaboration), and Reiteration.

blocks.title: Generic Structure Blueprint: Analytical Exposition
blocks.html:
1. Thesis (Urgent Context + Debatable Claim + Roadmap) → 2. Arguments (Point Sentences + Empirical Elaboration) → 3. Reiteration (Restated Thesis + Broader Synthesis)
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
1. Thesis StageIntroduces the anchoring issue and declares the author's central stance clearly.'Although costly to implement, urban vertical farming is indispensable for national food resilience.'
2. Argument BodyMultiple body paragraphs, each opening with a clear Topic Sentence backed by data.'Point 1: Insulation from weather volatility... Point 2: Reduction of transport freight emissions...'
3. Reiteration StageRestates the thesis using fresh vocabulary and evaluates broader societal implications.'In conclusion, investing in vertical agriculture transforms vulnerable cities into autonomous food hubs.'
Analytical vs HortatoryAnalytical convinces readers that a proposition IS true; Hortatory urges readers WHAT to do.Analytical ends with Reiteration; Hortatory ends with a Recommendation.

Pedagogical Note: An analytical exposition focuses on deconstructing reality to prove that an assertion is correct, without urging a direct plan of action.

blocks.title: Simulasi Interaktif: Dekonstruksi Argumen Teks Eksposisi
blocks.caption: Uji pemahaman Anda memisahkan klaim tesis, poin argumen pendukung, dan elaborasi data.

blocks.title: Ciri Khas Tesis yang Kuat
blocks.html: Tesis yang kuat tidak bersikap netral atau ragu-ragu. Penulis langsung memposisikan dirinya: 'Electric vehicles are a critical necessity for mitigating urban air pollution for three compelling reasons.'

lessons.title: Logical Connectors: Addition, Causation, Contrast, and Conclusion

blocks.html:
The Connective Tissue of Persuasive Prose

Logical connectors guide readers through the author's train of thought. Recognizing the precise function of each connector prevents you from misinterpreting whether the author is introducing an additional supporting argument, conceding a counterpoint, or delivering a final verdict.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Following the Flow of Logical Argumentation
blocks.html: Words like 'However', 'Furthermore', 'Consequently', and 'Notwithstanding' are not decorative filler. They are the traffic signposts of human thought. Misreading a single concessive transition like 'Although...' can invert your entire comprehension of which side the author actually supports!

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Halliday and Hasan on Cohesion in English
blocks.html:
Tokoh: M.A.K. Halliday & Ruqaiya Hasan Tahun: 1976 M Krisis: Students miss logical transitions between paragraphs, confusing an author's concession with their actual central stance.

Linguists M.A.K. Halliday and Ruqaiya Hasan published Cohesion in English (1976). They classified conjunctions into four primary logico-semantic categories: Additive, Adversative/Concessive, Causal/Explanatory, and Temporal.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Concessive, Adversative, and Causal Discourse Connectors
blocks.html:
Adversative / Concessive Connectors: Signal an acknowledgment of a counterpoint before pivoting back to the main stance (e.g., however, nonetheless, although, while it is true that).

Causal Connectors: Establish direct logical consequence and explanation (e.g., therefore, hence, consequently, as a result).

blocks.title: Argumentative Discourse Connector Taxonomy
blocks.html:
Additive (Reinforcing Stance) → Concessive (Acknowledging Counterpoint) → Causal (Drawing Logical Result) → Summative (Synthesizing Conclusion)
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Additive ConnectorsAdds new corroborating arguments in parallel.Furthermore, moreover, in addition, besides, additionally
Concessive Pivot MarkersSignals a turnabout: acknowledging an opposing fact without surrendering the thesis.However, nevertheless, nonetheless, despite this, on the other hand
Causal / Result MarkersEstablishes direct cause-and-effect relationship between premises.Consequently, therefore, thus, accordingly, as a direct outcome
Summative MarkersSignals the transition into final synthetic reiteration.In conclusion, to sum up, ultimately, in the final analysis

Pedagogical Note: When you see 'While / Although X, Y', the author's primary emphasis is ALWAYS on Y, while X is merely a subordinate concession.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Konjungsi Konsesif
blocks.question: Sentence: 'Admittedly, constructing renewable energy infrastructure demands high upfront capital; nevertheless, the long-term operational savings and health benefits far outweigh initial expenditures.' What is the author's primary argument?
steps: Klausa Konsesi ('Admittedly'): Penulis mengakui modal awal energi terbarukan memang mahal.
Konjungsi Penyelamat ('nevertheless'): Menegaskan kembali posisi utama penulis.
Klausa Argumen Utama: Penghematan operasional jangka panjang dan manfaat kesehatan jauh lebih besar daripada modal awal.
Simpulan: Penulis tetap mendukung penuh investasi energi terbarukan.
blocks.answer: Penulis mendukung pembangunan energi terbarukan karena manfaat jangka panjangnya melampaui biaya modal awalnya.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Which transition word is best suited to introduce an ADDITIONAL supportive reason in the third body paragraph of an analytical exposition?
blocks.hint: Additive connector untuk menambahkan poin sejalan adalah 'Furthermore'.
blocks.explanation: 'Furthermore' (terlebih lagi / selain itu) berfungsi menambahkan argumen penguat tambahan yang sejalan dengan tesis.

lessons.title: Separating Objective Evidence from Subjective Beliefs

blocks.html:
Evaluating Rhetorical Substantiation: Fact vs Opinion

An analytical essay is only as strong as its evidence. In the TKA exam, questions frequently ask you to distinguish between an empirical fact (which can be scientifically verified or proven) and a subjective value claim (which expresses the author's belief, feeling, or moral stance).

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Auditing Arguments for Factual Veracity
blocks.html: An editorial reads: 'Electric vehicle sales surged by 35% in 2024, proving that combustion engines are completely obsolete and evil.' The first clause (35% sales surge) is a verifiable statistical fact. The second clause (combustion engines are obsolete and evil) is a subjective value judgment. Critical readers must never conflate the two.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Toulmin on Evidence (Data) vs Claim
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Stephen Toulmin Tahun: 1958 M Krisis: Test-takers fail to distinguish between verifiable empirical evidence and an author's subjective value assertions.

Philosopher Stephen Toulmin (1958) established that a rational argument requires three structural components: Claim (the proposition being advanced), Grounds / Data (the objective facts supporting the claim), and Warrant (the logical bridge connecting data to claim).

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Empirical Fact vs Subjective Opinion in Argumentation
blocks.html:
Empirical Fact: Information that can be independently verified through third-party observation, scientific measurement, or official historical records.

Subjective Opinion: A personal interpretation, belief, feeling, or moral evaluation that cannot be definitively measured or proven true for all observers.

blocks.title: Fact vs Opinion Verification Protocol
blocks.html:
Locate Target Sentence → Check for Objective Measurability (Dates, Numbers, Studies) → Audit for Value-Laden Adjectives (Best, Terrible, Unacceptable) → Classify: Verifiable Metric vs Subjective Claim
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Empirical Fact'The global surface temperature rose by 1.1°C compared to pre-industrial baselines.'Can be cross-checked against NASA/NOAA scientific datasets.
Interpretive Opinion'This temperature rise demonstrates humanity's shameful disregard for creation.'Reflects an emotional and moral evaluation; cannot be measured physically.
Hybrid Statement'Solar costs dropped 80%, making clean energy the only moral choice.'Fact: 80% cost drop; Opinion: only moral choice.
Question StrategyWhen asked 'Which of the following expresses a fact rather than an opinion?'Select the option containing verifiable metrics and neutral reporting verbs.

Pedagogical Note: Words like 'obviously', 'undoubtedly', 'shockingly', and 'terrible' are clear linguistic markers of subjective opinion.

blocks.title: Contoh Membedakan Fakta dan Opini dalam Eksposisi
blocks.question: Paragraph: '(1) A 2023 study by Stanford researchers tracked 5,000 remote workers over two years. (2) The findings revealed that hybrid employees reported a 13% increase in productivity. (3) Therefore, remote working is unquestionably the single greatest blessing of modern corporate civilization.' Which sentence is a subjective opinion?
steps: Kalimat (1): Fakta penelitian terverifikasi (penelitian Stanford melacak 5.000 pekerja).
Kalimat (3): Opini subjektif hiperbolis ('unquestionably the single greatest blessing' adalah penilaian nilai emosional penulis).

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Which of the following sentences from an argumentative passage is an OBJECTIVE FACT?

options.A: Solar energy is undoubtedly superior to all other forms of power generation.
options.B: Photovoltaic cell manufacturing costs decreased by 85% between 2010 and 2020.
options.C: Every citizen ought to install solar panels to demonstrate environmental patriotism.
options.D: Traditional fossil fuel executives are deeply malicious individuals.

blocks.hint: Cari kalimat yang memuat data kuantitatif terverifikasi arsip sejarah/industri.
blocks.explanation: Penurunan biaya manufaktur sel surya sebesar 85% dalam kurun 2010-2020 adalah fakta empiris terverifikasi (objective fact).

lessons.title: Evaluating Argument Strength, Fallacies, and Author Credibility

blocks.html:
Critical Scrutiny: Detecting Logical Flaws in Arguments

Higher-level TKA questions test your evaluative competence by asking: 'Which of the following is the weakest point in the author’s argument?' or 'What logical assumption does the author rely on?'

To score high, you must recognize common rhetorical flaws (fallacies) in argumentative texts:

blocks.title: Real-World Context: Separating Strong Persuasion from Hollow Rhetoric
blocks.html: In parliamentary debates and university essays, shouting louder or using dramatic vocabulary does not make an argument strong. A truly strong argument relies on sound premises, sufficient representative sample sizes, and logical consistency that withstands hostile scrutiny.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Douglas Walton and Argumentation Schemes
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Douglas Walton Tahun: 2008 M Krisis: Learners judge an argument's strength by how passionate or angry the author sounds, rather than the soundness of its premises.

Logician Douglas Walton published Argumentation Schemes for Presumptive Reasoning (2008). Walton established standard critical questions to test whether an argument provides genuine presumptive weight or collapses into fallacious speculation.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Argument Strength, Validity, and Fallacy Vulnerability
blocks.html:
Argument Strength: The degree to which the premises provide compelling, logically coherent, and empirically verifiable grounds to accept the conclusion.

Argument Fallacy: An error in reasoning that invalidates the logical link between premises and conclusion.

blocks.title: Argument Strength Evaluation Heuristic
blocks.html:
Identify Central Conclusion → Audit Supporting Premises for Truth → Check Sample Size & Representativeness → Assess Vulnerability to Counterarguments
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
1. Premise VeracityAre the supporting factual claims verified by trustworthy sources?Reject unverified rumors or outdated statistics.
2. Logical RelevanceDo the premises actually relate directly to the conclusion?Spotting non-sequitur leaps and changing the subject.
3. Counter-Evidence ResilienceDoes the author anticipate and address obvious opposing evidence?Strong arguments openly address counterpoints.
4. Fallacy ScreenScreening for Hasty Generalization, Ad Hominem, and False Analogy.'My grandfather smoked and lived to 90' is NOT a valid epidemiological study.

Pedagogical Note: TKA evaluative questions test your ability to spot when an author makes a hasty generalization based on a single isolated anecdote.

blocks.title: Tiga Kesalahan Logika (Fallacies) dalam Teks Eksposisi
blocks.html:
1. Hasty Generalization: Menarik simpulan umum bagi seluruh populasi hanya berdasarkan 1 atau 2 sampel anekdotal kecil.
  2. False Dilemma (Either-Or Fallacy): Menyajikan situasi kompleks seolah-olah hanya memiliki dua pilihan ekstrem (misal: 'Either we ban all personal cars, or the planet is doomed').
  3. Post Hoc Ergo Propter Hoc: Mengasumsikan bahwa karena kejadian B terjadi setelah kejadian A, maka kejadian A pasti merupakan penyebab dari kejadian B.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Titik Lemah Argumen
blocks.question: Argument: 'My neighbor switched to a plant-based diet last month and immediately won a marathon. Therefore, plant-based nutrition guarantees elite athletic victory for anyone who adopts it.' What makes this argument weak?
steps: Dasar klaim: Pengalaman 1 orang tetangga (anekdotal individual tunggal).
Simpulan: 'guarantees elite athletic victory for anyone' (generalisasi tergesa-gesa / hasty generalization).
Faktor lain diabaikan: Jam latihan lari maraton, bakat genetik, usia, dan riwayat kesehatan tetangga tersebut sama sekali tidak dipertimbangkan.
blocks.answer: Argumen tersebut cacat karena melakukan hasty generalization dari satu sampel anekdot individual ke seluruh populasi.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: An author argues: 'Either our school bans smartphones entirely, or academic achievement will plummet to zero.' What logical fallacy is committed?
blocks.hint: Menyederhanakan masalah kompleks menjadi dua pilihan ekstrem adalah False Dilemma.
blocks.explanation: Penulis membatasi opsi menjadi dua kutub ekstrem ('larang sepenuhnya atau nilai hancur total') tanpa mempertimbangkan jalan tengah pemanfaatan edukatif (False Dilemma).

lessons.title: Addressing Counterarguments and Author Stance Modifications

blocks.html:
Counterarguments and Rebuttals: The Mark of Rigorous Persuasion

The strongest analytical essays do not ignore opposing viewpoints. Instead, the author introduces a counterargument (the opposing camp's perspective) and then delivers an effective rebuttal (explaining why that counterargument is insufficient, outdated, or flawed).

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The Power of 'Steel-Manning' Your Opponent
blocks.html: In elite debate and academic publishing, the most formidable thinkers do not pretend their opponents do not exist. They 'steel-man' the counterargument—presenting the opposing camp's objection in its strongest possible form—and then systematically dismantle it with superior empirical evidence.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: John Swales and Rhetorical Moves in Academic Writing
blocks.html:
Tokoh: John Swales Tahun: 1990 M Krisis: Students think acknowledging an opposing viewpoint weakens their essay, failing to see that concession-rebuttal pairs strengthen authorial authority.

Linguist John Swales (1990) demonstrated that professional academic writers establish their scholarly authority (ethos) by executing the Concession-Rebuttal Rhetorical Move: acknowledging an alternative hypothesis before proving its inadequacy.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: Concession, Rebuttal, and Dialectical Staging
blocks.html:
Concession: The strategic acknowledgment of an opposing argument, limitation, or counter-evidence.

Rebuttal: The subsequent argumentation that refutes, minimizes, or overturns the conceded point with superior logic or updated data.

blocks.title: Concession-Rebuttal Architectural Staging
blocks.html:
Concession Stems ('Admittedly...', 'Critics argue that...') → Pivot Marker ('However...', 'Nonetheless...') → Rebuttal ('Recent longitudinal data demonstrates...')
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Step 1: Fair ConcessionAcknowledging the opposing claim with intellectual honesty.'Admittedly, transitioning to nuclear power involves substantial upfront capital costs...'
Step 2: Pivot TransitionSignaling the turnabout back to the author's primary thesis.'However, this financial hurdle is dramatically offset when...'
Step 3: Decisive RebuttalSupplying decisive evidence that overturns the objection.'...when lifetime operational lifespans and zero-carbon grid stability are factored into the lifecycle cost.'
Question StrategyWhen asked 'Why does the author mention [opposing view] in paragraph 3?'The correct answer is: To acknowledge a counterpoint before demonstrating its limitations.

Pedagogical Note: Recognize that when an author presents a counterargument, they are preparing to deliver a rebuttal, NOT changing their overall stance.

blocks.title: Contoh Analisis Counterargument dan Rebuttal
blocks.question: Passage: 'Skeptics argue that high-speed rail projects impose prohibitive financial debt on developing nations. While initial capital investment is undeniably massive, longitudinal economic analyses show that secondary regional development, reduced highway maintenance, and industrial corridor expansion offset construction costs within twelve years.' What is the author doing in this paragraph?
steps: Klaim Lawan (Counterargument): Kereta cepat membebani utang besar pada negara berkembang.
Rebuttal Penulis: Analisis longitudinal membuktikan manfaat ekonomi sekunder dan koridor industri menutup modal awal dalam 12 tahun.
Fungsi Retorika: Mematahkan argumen skeptis dengan menyajikan data manfaat ekonomi jangka panjang.
blocks.answer: Penulis membantah (rebuts) kekhawatiran finansial pihak lawan dengan data kompensasi ekonomi sekunder jangka panjang.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: In an analytical exposition, what is the primary rhetorical function of introducing a COUNTERARGUMENT followed by a REBUTTAL?

options.A: To confuse the reader about where the author stands.
options.B: To demonstrate that the issue has no possible solution.
options.C: To strengthen the author's primary thesis by proactively refuting potential objections.
options.D: To increase the overall word count of the essay.

blocks.hint: Counterargument dan rebuttal memperkuat tesis utama.
blocks.explanation: Memasukkan argumen tandingan dan melumpuhkannya dengan sanggahan ilmiah memperkuat kredibilitas dan ketangguhan tesis utama penulis.

lessons.title: Jebakan Distraktor Argumen: Pilihan yang Benar Secara Fakta Tetapi Tidak Relevan

blocks.html:
The Deadliest Distractor in TKA Expository Reading: Factual but Irrelevant

In high-difficulty analytical reading items, test creators will present an option that is 100% scientifically true and verified in the real world. However, it is the wrong answer because it does not directly address the author's primary thesis or the specific question stem.

blocks.title: Real-World Context: The 'True in Real Life, but Irrelevant to the Text' Trap
blocks.html: Suppose you are reading an essay arguing that high-speed rail reduces intercity highway traffic. One of the multiple-choice options reads: 'Exercise improves cardiovascular health.' Is exercise good for your heart? Absolutely, it is 100% true in real life! But does it support the author's claim about trains? Not at all! This is the most seductive trap in standardized reading tests.

blocks.title: Historical Insight: Robert Ebel on Psychometric Item Distractor Design
blocks.html:
Tokoh: Robert L. Ebel Tahun: 1972 M Krisis: Test-takers pick options that are factually true in real life, failing to realize that the statement is completely irrelevant to the author's actual passage argument.

Psychometrician Robert L. Ebel (1972) classified multiple-choice distractors. He proved that high-discriminating items use distractors containing universally accepted real-world truths that lack textual warrant, exposing whether candidates are reading the passage or relying on general knowledge bias.

blocks.title: Conceptual Definition: The Three Major Distractor Archetypes in TKA Reading
blocks.html:
1. Factual but Irrelevant Trap: Statements that are true in the real world but have no logical bearing on the passage's argument.

2. Extreme Extrapolation Trap: Exaggerating the author's hedged claim into an absolute imperative.

3. Opposite Claim Trap: Inverting a subtle negative or concessive marker.

blocks.title: Distractor Elimination Protocol
blocks.html:
Read Question Stem Carefully → Cross-Check Candidate Option with Passage Lines → Check: Does the Text Actually Support This Claim? → Eliminate Unwarranted Real-World Bias
Tahap / KomponenFungsi Retoris / MaknaCiri Kebahasaan / Contoh Penerapan
Trap 1: Factual but IrrelevantStatement is scientifically true in real life, but the author never mentioned it.Eliminate immediately: Test evaluates reading comprehension, not trivia recall.
Trap 2: Absolute ModifiersPassage says 'often helps' → Option says 'invariably guarantees success'Eliminate options with 'always', 'only', 'never', 'solely' unless explicitly warranted.
Trap 3: Half-Truth DistortionFirst half of option is accurate; second half injects a false assumption.Verify the entire option through to the final word.
Trap 4: Verbatim Word MatchOption repeats 5 exact words from paragraph 1, but twists the grammatical meaning.Beware verbatim word-matching traps; look for accurate paraphrases instead.

Pedagogical Note: Always demand direct textual warrant. If a claim cannot be proven from the passage text itself, it is an incorrect option on TKA English.

blocks.title: Cara Menghindari Jebakan 'Factual but Irrelevant'
blocks.html:
Ketika membaca opsi jawaban, jangan hanya bertanya: 'Apakah kalimat ini benar?'
Tanyakanlah: 'Apakah kalimat ini menjawab argumen pokok yang diminta oleh stem soal?'

blocks.title: Contoh Membedah Jebakan Fakta Tak Relevan
blocks.question: Question: 'What is the author's main argument regarding public transit investment?' Passage Focus: Public buses and trains dramatically lower greenhouse gas emissions per passenger-kilometer. Options: (A) Electric trains travel faster than traditional steam engines. (B) Expanding public transit networks is a vital measure to combat urban carbon emissions. (C) Bus drivers must undergo rigorous licensing examinations.
steps: Evaluasi (A): Benar secara sejarah sains, tetapi sama sekali tidak relevan dengan argumen emisi gas rumah kaca.
Evaluasi (C): Benar di dunia nyata, tetapi merupakan detail administratif yang tidak ada kaitannya dengan tesis lingkungan.
Evaluasi (B): Benar dan langsung menjawab tesis inti teks.

blocks.title: Cek Pemahaman
blocks.question: Why would an answer choice stating 'Water boils at 100°C at sea level' be an invalid answer to a question asking for the main argument of an essay on hydroelectric dams?

options.A: Because water does not boil at 100°C.
options.B: Because although it is a scientific fact, it has no logical relevance to the author's argument on hydroelectric energy.
options.C: Because the sentence contains passive voice syntax.
options.D: Because it contradicts the author's personal philosophy.

blocks.hint: Fakta ilmiah yang tidak relevan dengan topik tesis adalah distraktor jebakan.
blocks.explanation: Pilihan tersebut adalah fakta ilmiah objektif, tetapi tidak memiliki relevansi logis dengan argumen pembangunan bendungan hidroelektrik (factual but irrelevant).

lessons.title: Analytical Argument Assessment and Chapter Quiz

blocks.html:
Analytical Exposition Mastery Review

Integrate your argument analysis toolkit before undertaking the official chapter quiz:

  • Locate the thesis in the opening paragraph and restatement in the reiteration.
  • Trace logical connectors (additive, adversative, causal) to follow argument momentum.
  • Separate verifiable empirical statistics from subjective value judgments and fallacies.
  • Eliminate true-in-reality but irrelevant distractor choices.

blocks.title: Simulasi Ujian
blocks.html: Kuis terdiri atas 20 butir soal terstandar yang menganalisis isu-isu global kontemporer (perubahan iklim, literasi digital, ekonomi sirkular).

blocks.title: Cheat Sheet: Analytical Exposition & Argument Persuasion
blocks.subtitle: Summary of thesis, supporting arguments, reiteration, persuasive rhetorical markers, and connective logic.
blocks.html:
1. Generic Structure

  • Thesis: Introduces the controversial topic and clearly posits the writer's stance/point of view.
  • Arguments (Body Paragraphs): Each paragraph presents one core premise supported by empirical evidence, data, or expert reasoning.
  • Reiteration / Conclusion: Restates the thesis in new words and summarizes the cumulative arguments.

2. Transition Discourse Connectors

Rhetorical FunctionKey Transition Words
Reinforcing / AdditionFurthermore, Moreover, In addition, Not to mention
Contrast / CounterpointHowever, Conversely, On the other hand, Nonetheless
Cause & ConsequenceConsequently, Therefore, As a result, Thus, Hence
ExemplificationFor instance, To illustrate, Specifically, Namely
